# Anis Benyoub

> Anis Benyoub builds renderers: ray tracing, volumetric clouds and the water system in Unity's HDRP, GPU research at Intel, and Nyx at Genesis AI, where he leads graphics.

Site: {{ site.url }}/
Email: {{ site.author.email }}
GitHub: {{ site.github }}
LinkedIn: {{ site.linkedin }}
X: {{ site.twitter }}
Location: Paris, France

## Who I am

At Genesis AI, I wrote the first version of Nyx, the in-house renderer of Genesis World, and carried it through to release. Nyx targets robotics training and simulation and combines several rendering pipelines: a path tracer for high-fidelity output, a rasterization pipeline and hybrid rendering. It shipped with Genesis World 1.0 in May 2026 (https://github.com/Genesis-Embodied-AI/genesis-world) and is available on PyPI as gs-nyx (https://pypi.org/project/gs-nyx/), with the Genesis integration plugin as gs-nyx-plugin (https://pypi.org/project/gs-nyx-plugin/).

Once the initial technology was in place, I built the graphics team around it: engineers, technical artists and artists. I also lead the company's digital twin effort.

From 2023 to 2025, I was a research engineer at Intel GPU Research in Paris, in the Grenoble GraphiX (GGX) research team (https://ggx-research.github.io/). My public work there covered real-time rendering, adaptive geometry, sampling and neural texture compression.

From 2018 to 2023, I was a senior graphics engineer at Unity Technologies and one of the main contributors to the High Definition Render Pipeline (HDRP). Among other features, I built its real-time ray tracing and the hybrid raster/ray tracing pipeline, the volumetric clouds, the water system and screen-space global illumination.

Earlier, I was a graphics engineer at Pretty Simple Games, and a software engineer at Autodesk on 3ds Max, Autodesk LIVE and the Stingray game engine. I hold an M.Sc. in Computer Science from Polytechnique Montréal and an M.Eng. in Computer Science from INSA Lyon.

Areas of expertise: path tracing, real-time rendering, GPU performance, adaptive geometry, neural texture compression, rendering for robotics simulation.

## Career timeline

- July 2025–present: Genesis AI, Paris. Graphics Lead: wrote the first version of Nyx and carried it to release (multi-pipeline renderer for robotics training and simulation: path tracing, rasterization, hybrid rendering; part of Genesis World 1.0, May 2026); then built and leads the graphics team (engineers, technical artists and artists) and the digital twin effort.
- February 2023–July 2025: Intel Corporation, GPU Research, Paris. Graphics and AI research engineer in the Grenoble GraphiX (GGX) research team, https://ggx-research.github.io/ (real-time rendering, adaptive geometry, sampling, neural texture compression).
- August 2018–January 2023: Unity Technologies, Paris. Senior graphics engineer, one of the main contributors to the High Definition Render Pipeline (HDRP): real-time ray tracing, hybrid raster/ray tracing pipeline, volumetric clouds, water system, SSGI.
- August 2017–July 2018: Pretty Simple Games, Paris. Graphics engineer.
- May 2015–August 2017: Autodesk, Montréal then Paris. Software engineer (3ds Max, Autodesk LIVE, Stingray game engine).
- Internships: Eugen Systems, Paris (2013); CNRS, Lyon (2012).
- Education: M.Sc. Computer Science, Polytechnique Montréal (2013–2015); M.Eng. Computer Science, INSA Lyon (2009–2015).
